title: The perfect 4th
summary: Some intervals have one plain, stable size, called perfect. The first is the 4th.

steps.title: Perfect intervals
steps.body:
The 4th, the 5th and the octave have one main size, and it sounds so open and stable that it is called **perfect**. They do not come in minor and major.

**Why it matters:** When someone says "a perfect 4th", the word perfect tells you it is the plain, stable version of that interval.

steps.title: Perfect 4th
steps.body:
A **perfect 4th** is 5 half steps and spans four letters, like C to F.

**Why it matters:** It is the sound of Here Comes the Bride, and of many bass lines that jump around a song.

steps.title: A 4th from D
steps.body: D up to G is also a perfect 4th: 5 half steps.

items.prompt: Play C4, then go up a perfect 4th.
Play D4, then go up a perfect 4th.

Play A4, then go up a perfect 4th.

steps.title: Open sound
steps.body: Play a perfect 4th with both notes together, then move it around the white keys. Most of them sound open; listen for the one starting on F, which sounds different. You will meet it in two lessons.
